Review the README.md and /src files for repository details. .NET 10.0 (`net10.0`); latest C#; nullable, implicit usings, warnings-as-errors. Layout: src/, tests/, Directory.Build.props, Directory.Packages.props, Template.slnx. Central Package Management: package versions in Directory.Packages.props; project references without versions. When adding a new package: Add `<PackageVersion Include="PackageName" Version="x.y.z" />` to [Directory.Packages.props](Directory.Packages.props).

Use file-scoped namespaces; `_camelCase` private fields, PascalCase constants, `I` interfaces, `Async` suffixes, `var` where apparent. **Code Blocks**: Always use `{}` for blocks except single-line exits (e.g., `return`, `throw`). 2-space indentation; CRLF; UTF-8 BOM. **Braces**: Always use braces for control flow (`csharp_prefer_braces = true`). Allman braces; primary constructors assigned to readonly fields; top-level statements; pattern matching; expression-bodied properties/accessors, not methods. Run `dotnet format`; use [Directory.Build.props](Directory.Build.props) analyzers.

Configuration: appsettings.json, appsettings.{Environment}.json, IConfiguration, IOptions<T>, typed settings; User Secrets. Never hardcode sensitive information in source code. Use Microsoft.Extensions.Logging and structured, contextual, level-appropriate logs. Avoid logging sensitive information. Follow OWASP guidelines for secure coding practices. Validate and sanitize all user inputs. Use parameterized queries or ORM features to prevent SQL injection. Implement proper authentication and authorization mechanisms. Use HTTPS for all communications. Use Ardalis.GuardClauses for non-UI validation; prefer FluentValidation for complex/UI validation; return suitable HTTP errors.

Write testable, focused, DI-based code; prefer composition, async I/O, short methods and argument lists. Prefer REPR/FastEndpoints and DDD; API *Request/*Response, use-case *Command/*Query, DTO *Details/*Summary; avoid exposing domain entities or colocating interfaces and implementations.

New projects: production in src/, tests in tests/; xUnit. `dotnet run --project src/YourProject/YourProject.csproj`. Use `xUnit` for all tests. Only test code that you control and that has business logic; do not test framework code. Arrange-Act-Assert with whitespace; mirror features. Do not name test classes with "Tests" suffix; do use "Tests" suffix for folder names if needed. Name test classes `ClassName_MethodName.cs`; methods `DoesSomething_GivenSomeCondition`; use `[Fact]`, `[Theory]`, `[InlineData]`. Prefer NSubstitute and Shouldly. Avoid commercially licensed testing libraries (e.g. FluentAssertions, Moq).

Use Markdown headings and highlighted snippets; lint docs. Lists and code listings should always have a blank line before and after them.
